messages:
neha: Quick flag — after yesterday's tokenizer roll (tokenizerv2.1) + tiny system prompt change, /generate prefix cache hit rate for prod service dropped ~78% -> ~41%. Noticed increased tail latency and more KV lookups.

javier: :eyes: timeline? which deploy introduced the tokenizer bump vs the prompt tweak?

neha: Deploy order was tokenizer bump at 02:10, system prompt patch at 02:34 (just added a "context_version" line to system prompt for audit). First metrics spike at 02:45.

liz: Do we have a quick repro that shows different cache keys for effectively same user prompt? If tokenizer change changed token boundaries, keys could diverge.

tyler: I pulled a sample of 5k requests around the window. Two similar prompts differ only in trailing space after a function block and they produced different token sequences with v2.1. Example: 
```
old tokenizer tokens: [502, 14, 9003, 2]
new tokenizer tokens: [502, 14, 9003, 12, 2]
```
That extra token breaks the KV prefix match.

sam: Also noticed our cache key includes the raw system prompt text + tool metadata JSON. Small audit fields like "context_version" change the key. We treat system prompt as part of key.

javier: Ugh. So two orthogonal causes: tokenizer granularity change and system-prompt churn. Any quick mitigations?

neha: Short-term: roll back tokenizerv2.1 for prod or pin tokenizer version in the cache key so warmup is consistent. Mid-term: canonicalize cache key. Options: normalize whitespace, strip ephemeral audit fields from system prompt, and use a tokenizer-invariant signature.

liz: For canonicalization proposal, I ran a small script that normalizes prompts by: trim(), collapse-multi-space -> single, remove trailing punctuation on system prompt audit fields, and stable-sort tool keys. It increased hit rate on sample by +22% when applied offline.

tyler: Script snippet I used to diff tokenization: 
```python
def canonical_prompt(p):
    p = ' '.join(p.strip().split())
    # remove audit kvs
    p = re.sub(r'context_version:\s*\S+', '', p)
    return p
```
Then hashed canonical_prompt + model+tokenizer_version for cache key.

sam: Hashing model+tokenizer_version is important. If we don't, changes are silent and warmup mismatches happen. But do we want to bake tokenizer into key? That prevents cross-version reuse but avoids silent incompatibility.

javier: Another angle: prefill/warmup jobs can be made tokenizer-aware. If we detect tokenizer version bump, trigger background warmup to repopulate prefixes with new keys. That would avoid falling back. Implement detection in rollout pipeline.

neha: Agreed. Proposed immediate action list:
1) Add tokenizer_version to cache key metadata (short term).
2) Implement prompt canonicalization rules (whitespace, stable tool field ordering, drop audit-only fields) and run as A/B for a week.
3) Add rollout hook to enqueue targeted warmup for changed tokenizer or system prompt diffs.
4) Run a one-off patch to backfill heavy prefixes for last 7 days if we keep tokenizer bump.

liz: Caveat: canonicalization must be conservative — don't remove semantic tokens (e.g., JSON tool payloads). Only drop audit fields and normalize spacing. We'll need unit tests on many prompt shapes.

tyler: Also check batching heuristics: we route requests into batch buckets by prefix-length histogram. If canonicalization changes token counts, batching distribution might shift. Need to profile kernel selection for prevalent sequence lengths post-change.

sam: Good call — I saw a small regression in fastpath kernel usage for sequences ~64-72 tokens after this change. Could be due to token boundary shifts.

javier: For immediate rollout: neha, can you open a small PR that adds tokenizer_version to the cache key and a feature flag for canonicalization? We can rollout the flag to 10% first.

neha: On it. I will also add a metric to console: cache_hit_rate_by_tokenizer_version and cache_warmup_repopulation_latency.

build-bot: deploy-notice: canary rollout triggered for eng-runtime at 04:05 by neha (feature-flag:cache-canonicalization=10%).

javier: After canary we should run the replay test against prod logs to estimate warmup time for hot prefixes. If warmup is slow, we'll need an active backfill job that uses the actual tokenizer to precompute KV entries.

liz: I'll write tests for canonicalization edgecases — JSON payload, function call proto, and triple-backtick fences. Will push by EOD.

tyler: I'll re-run kernel-selection perf harness for 64-128 token bins with tokenizerv2.1 to confirm no regression once warmup completes.

neha: Thanks team. If we see >10% hit rate improvement in canary -> promote. If not, rollback tokenizer bump.

sam: Also add a note in runbook for oncall: when cache hit rate drops quickly after deploy, check tokenizer_version diffs and system prompt diffs before assuming runtime regressions.

javier: Solid. We'll reconvene in 1h after canary metrics. :thumbsup:
